2609.15773.title: Transfer Learning for Socioeconomic Estimation in Forced-Displacement Settings
2609.15773.paper_summary: Progress in inclusive household surveys has strengthened socioeconomic evidence for forcibly displaced populations, providing indispensable benchmarks on living conditions and welfare. However, these surveys remain resource-intensive and periodic, while conditions can change between rounds, particularly in settings affected by fragility, conflict, and violence. More frequently updated, spatially granular complementary evidence is therefore needed to identify where socioeconomic conditions may be changing between survey rounds and to inform operational prioritization. Earth observation and machine learning offer a scalable source of spatially explicit socioeconomic information. However, tools developed for general populations have not been systematically adapted and evaluated in forced displacement settings, where living conditions, settlement patterns, and displacement impacts may differ substantially. We address this gap by adapting a multimodal spatiotemporal vision transformer, pretrained on Demographic and Health Survey data from approximately 1.2 million households across 36 African countries, to forced displacement and host community settings in South Sudan, Cameroon, and Zambia. We develop and evaluate the updated, adapted model using socioeconomic indices derived from UNHCR FDS and RMS data. Our results show that satellite-derived geospatial covariates explain up to 66% of the variation in socioeconomic outcomes in camp-intersecting grids, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.37 index points, and 41% in non-camp-intersecting areas, with an MAE of 5.41. The framework complements and adds value to periodic household surveys by filling critical spatial and temporal data gaps with regularly updated, model-based socioeconomic estimates. These estimates sustain insight between survey rounds and support timely humanitarian prioritization and field verification.
2609.15773.paper_summary_zh: 包容性家庭調查的進展增強了對被迫流離失所人口的社會經濟證據，提供了有關生活條件和福利的不可或缺的基準。<lb/>然而，這些調查仍然資源密集且周期性，條件可能在不同輪次之間發生變化，特別是在受到脆弱性、衝突和暴力影響的環境中。因此，需要更頻繁更新、空間上細緻的補充證據，以識別社會經濟條件在調查輪次之間可能發生變化的地方，並為操作優先級提供信息。<lb/>地球觀測和機器學習提供了一個可擴展的空間明確社會經濟信息來源。<lb/>然而，為一般人群開發的工具尚未在被迫流離失所的環境中進行系統性的調整和評估，因為那裡的生活條件、安置模式和流離失所影響可能有很大不同。<lb/>我們通過將一個多模態時空視覺Transformer進行調整，該Transformer在來自36個非洲國家的約120萬戶家庭的《人口與健康調查》數據上進行了預訓練，來填補這一空白，並應用於南蘇丹、喀麥隆和贊比亞的被迫流離失所和接待社區環境。<lb/>我們使用來自UNHCR FDS和RMS數據的社會經濟指數開發並評估了更新的調整模型。<lb/>我們的結果顯示，衛星衍生的地理空間協變量解釋了營地交叉網格中社會經濟結果變異的高達66%，平均絕對誤差（MAE）為4.37指數點，而在非營地交叉區域中為41%，MAE為5.41。<lb/>該框架通過用定期更新的基於模型的社會經濟估計填補關鍵的空間和時間數據缺口，從而補充並增值於周期性家庭調查。<lb/>這些估計在調查輪次之間持續提供見解，並支持及時的人道主義優先級和現場驗證。
